predecessors.name: West Francia
predecessors.text: 'The Treaty of Meerssen mentions the comitatus Hainoum, a county, and granted it to the western kingdom' (870); infobox 'Consolidation of county: ±880'

successors.name: Duchy of Burgundy
successors.text: 'Absorbed into the Burgundian Netherlands: 1432'; 'In 1432 Jacqueline had to cede the inheritance rights of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland to Duke Philip'

ledger.x: 1254: the second arbitration of Louis IX.
1432: 'Jacqueline had to cede the inheritance rights of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland to Duke Philip'.

wars.name: War of the Succession of Flanders and Hainault
wars.outcome: Louis IX awarded Hainaut to John I of Avesnes in 1246; Avesnes won the battle of West-Capelle on 4 July 1253 and the second arbitration of 1254 left him 'secure in Hainault'; 'Flanders passed to the Dampierres'.

wars.name: Jacqueline's war over Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland
wars.outcome: Humphrey of Gloucester was recognised as count of Hainaut on 5 December 1424; John III of Bavaria died on 6 January 1425; the Treaty of Delft (3 July 1428) left Jacqueline her titles with Philip as heir.

certainty.note: The pages give counts, treaties and towns, not boundaries; the outline is the Belgian province with two French circles.
